issue.title: Skill-use detail lane still caches whole-project SkillUseEvent snapshots (11.4k live objects)

task_type_fields.impact: Long-lived TUI sessions retain every skill-use event of each cached project (about 11k objects on athena and growing with the log), which feeds the chronic gen-2 heap that sase-1nc tracks. Each refresh after a log change reparses the whole file.
task_type_fields.repro:
`src/sase/ace/tui/skill_uses.py` still keeps a module-level `_skill_uses_snapshot_cache` (`BoundedLRUCache[str, _SkillUsesSnapshotCacheEntry]`). Each entry holds every `SkillUseEvent` in a project's skill-use log (`_load_skill_use_events_snapshot` -> `read_skill_use_events(project=...)`) so that the per-agent lane can filter in Python. sase-1t3.11.1 replaced this exact pattern for `memory_reads.jsonl` and `artifact_reads.jsonl` with streamed, targeted per-agent/context queries in sase-core (see `src/sase/ace/tui/memory_reads.py` and `src/sase/ace/tui/artifact_reads.py`, with caches capped at 128 x 50 rows). The skill-use lane was not in that phase's named scope.

Evidence: the post-storm GC census in sase-1t3.9 (note #5, 2 h sample, instance 39893a35, `~/.sase/perf/sase-1t3.9/gc_census_20261117T145641Z`) found 11,402 live `sase.skills.use_log.SkillUseEvent` objects (0.55 MB). That matched `_skill_uses_snapshot_cache` at 11,397 events, so the cache was effectively the only owner.

Fix: give skill uses the same targeted per-agent and context query shape as memory reads. Use a sase-core streamed filter plus binding and pin move if this is shared behavior, otherwise a streamed Python reader. Keep stat-before-query with the 0.5 s throttle, and delete the full-log snapshot cache. Add a retention test showing that unrelated events are not materialized.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by sase-1t3.9 note #5 (post-storm GC census); sase-1t3.11 bounded the sibling memory and artifact read logs but left the skill-use whole-file cache in place.
